pins.name: D15
pins.label: D15 (GPIO15)
pins.notes: Vendor-documented special purpose during device reset — GroundStudio's own datasheet recommends against using GP15 in your projects (no further technical detail published).

pins.name: GPIO16
pins.label: GPIO16
pins.notes:
PIN_SPI0_MISO — onboard microSD card adapter's SPI0 data-in line, connected by default. Not general-purpose in the board's as-shipped configuration. Confirmed via the official GroundStudio Marble Pico Datasheet ('adapter for micro-SD type memory cards connected to the SPI0 port (default)... the adapter can be disconnected using the solder jumpers on the back of the pcb'). No spi_miso auto-tag applies (this board's pins_arduino.h declares no bare `static const uint8_t MISO` alias for build_boards.js's bus-role auto-append to key off).
Check if available on board

pins.name: GPIO24
pins.label: GPIO24
pins.notes:
PIN_VBAT / PIN_SD_SWITCH — solder-jumper (J17) selected internal-hardware line: either the onboard 1-cell LiPo charging circuit's default connection, or (J17 alternative position) the microSD adapter's card-presence switch. Not a general-purpose header-broken-out GPIO in either jumper position. Confirmed via this board's own pins_arduino.h inline comments ('J17 Default Connection' / 'J17 Alternative Connection') read together with the official datasheet's schematic ('1 cell 3.7-4.2V battery charging circuit' block); exact active-high/low polarity for either mode is not published, so no capability is asserted beyond exclusion from general GPIO use.
Check if available on board

pins.name: GPIO25
pins.label: GPIO25 (Led active high)
pins.notes:
PIN_LED — onboard user LED, active-high. Confirmed verbatim via the official GroundStudio Marble Pico Datasheet: 'There is a built-in LED controlled by the GP25 pin. When the pin is HIGH or LOW, the LED is on and off, respectively.' digital_input dropped to match this repo's established led_high precedent for dedicated onboard LED pins (rpipico, adafruit_feather_adalogger); pwm_output kept since arduino-pico's analogWrite() works on any RP2040 GPIO, enabling brightness dimming.
Check if available on board
